title: Ariamis
snippet: The Painted World of Ariamis was protected by an order of Painting Guardians. Anor Londo benefited from the Painted World as a prison for the spurned; it served as a place to seal away dangerous artifacts, abominations, sinners and Hollows. Velka, following from her role as the Goddess of Sin, eventually spread her influence inside the Painted World, where dozens of her cultist followers found refuge. Crossbreed Priscilla considered herself a guardian of the Painted World which she characterized as "peaceful". She pitied the "kind" inhabitants of the painting, as the outside world had shunned and locked them away, like herself. Priscilla became the "Lady" of the Painted World and its inhabitants, and welcomed the forlorn who were led into the cold world by the heretical tales of corvian storytellers. The humanoid corvians who found refuge in the Painting formed a small village, complete with knights and a library.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Birch Woman
snippet:
Birch Woman -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The real threat provided by these enemies is their camouflage. It is possible to determine whether a Birch Woman is dangerous by looking directly at the hair on their heads. If the hair stands still, it is not an enemy, but if it move slightly because of the wind, then it is an enemy.

Even though they are slow enemies, they must not be underestimated because they are often found near other faster enemies, such as Wolves. They provide ranged support for these enemies, and can be problematic if not dealt with.

As soon as a Birch Woman is recognized, the player can simply run and kill it. The player shouldn't be greedy; attack them from behind, as to prevent their grab attack. In about three to four hits they should be down. If they are hit with Fire damage, they will catch fire and scream, becoming incapacitated.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Gravetender will walk up after a short time (his footprints will be visible through the fog). Once he is there, cast Poison or Toxic Mist again, until his health bar begins to shrink. Be aware that he can shoot sorceries through the fog and they can hit you. Once he is dead, in order to spawn the Greatwolf, you have to make your way all the way up to the chapel (warping via a bonfire resets the fight) and down into the basement with the Giant Flies until the howl of the Greatwolf is heard, then run all the way back to the fog wall of the boss fight, and repeat the cheese on the wolf as with the Gravetender. However, since the trip is long and arduous and the flies are particularly dangerous, you can just enter the fog after the man dies (the prompt appears when close to it) and deal with the wolf in normal combat. The wolf will appear near the building, as soon as the fog wall is entered.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The ideal strategy during the second phase is to try to finish off the Gravetender as quickly as possible, to remove the Greatwolf's support and ensure that there is only one enemy to focus on. A good tactic to minimize exposure to the Greatwolf's attacks is to lure it around the pillars of the large tower in the arena; this works particularly well against its charging attacks as the pillars provide cover against them as well as deflecting the Greatwolf away from the player. This can allow the player to avoid the Greatwolf's attacks, and buy time to maneuver around to engage the Gravetender alone.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : It is advised to kill the three wolves that accompany the Champion's Gravetender at the beginning of the fight as to ensure they do not become problematic when facing him head on. The Gravetender will fight very aggressively, using his sword and shield's unique combination attacks to strike while blocking, turning each attempt to attack him into a trade that minimizes damage to himself. For this reason, it is not suggested to use small arms such as straight swords to fight him, but rather to use bigger weapons such as an ultra greatsword to inflict heavy stagger on him and to break his guard to open him up to ripostes. He is weak against Lightning and Bleed, which might be good to keep in mind.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: They will only be relieved of their duty by the Ashen One, who finds their way to the bottom of the painting and challenges the duo to partake in the old turnament of the champion. All that is known is that the old champion's remains would find their way in the possession of Amnesiac Lapp during the collapse of the world into the Dreg Heap.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - exploit 
 exploit : It is possible to cheese the fight against the boss: from the Depths of the Painting bonfire, approach the ledge around the arena, but do not hop down. Instead, equip the Black Bow of Pharis and the Hawk Ring, plus Feather Arrows. The bow paired with the ring and standard arrows doesn't work for the cheese, as they don't go far enough. Zoom in and there will be a wolf visible to the right, next to a column. Shoot at it to aggro it and the fog wall will appear. Step back at this point and cast poison Mist or Toxic Mist around the area where you just stood. Three wolves at the base of the short cliff will get poisoned and their diminishing health bars will appear visible behind the wall.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - plot 
 plot : The Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf are an easy to miss optional encounter found within the *Ashes of Ariandel DLC*.

The fight starts off with just the Champion's Gravetender and three wolves. Once his health has been halved, he will call for the Greatwolf by performing the "By my sword" gesture, making the fight a lot more challenging. Defeating both enemies here allows the player to obtain the Champion's Bones. By burning them at the bonfire in Firelink Shrine, they'll be able to unlock the Undead Match, a type of PvP mode. Beating the boss also results in obtaining Valorheart, which could be the player's only reward if they've somehow found the Champion's Bones already by exploring *The Ringed City DLC* first.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Greatwolf, on the other hand, fights very aggressively and will perform a charging attack very similar to that of Vordt of the Boreal Valley, albeit much faster. It's not advised to block these attacks with anything less than a greatshield, as they can devastate the player's stamina, leading to a guard break and an almost guaranteed hit from the Greatwolf. Once the Greatwolf is at 50% health, it will perform a howl and its eyes will glow red. At this point the Greatwolf gains a Frost breath attack and becomes even faster and more aggressive. It shares the same weaknesses to Lightning and Bleed as its master, with an added Fire weakness. Most of these strategies also apply to its solo appearances outside the boss fight, though one must be aware of the amount of normal wolves that may turn the tides in the beast's favor in those situations.

snippet:
Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : The and the are an optional duo boss in the *Dark Souls III: Ashes of Ariandel DLC*. The Greatwolf also appears as a powerful enemy outside of the designated boss fight.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: location : The boss fight is found in an optional location of the Painted World of Ariandel. The player must destroy the rickety bridge that leads to the chapel from the side of said chapel, which will then allow them to climb down using the bridge's remains, like in the Catacombs of Carthus. From there, they must descend using the large roots jutting out of the cliffside, fending off Farron Followers and avoiding the exploding arrows that are shot by the two Millwood Knights below. After reaching the bottom, one can find the Depths of the Painting bonfire by proceeding forward from the last root where one of the Millwood Knights stood. From there, the boss fight can be reached by turning right and dropping down into the flower field opposite from the side of the frozen lake with Frost Crabs. The Champion's Gravetender will be found beneath a building resembling Crossbreed Priscilla's old battle arena from *Dark Souls*.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: The Champion of the Undead Match eventually went mad, ending up in the Painted World of Ariandel as a result. Only his page and a large wolf stayed by his side, until the day he finally died. The champion was buried in the lower section of the painting, where a small tombstone is still guarded by the very same page and wolf that had remained with him in his madness. They became guardians of that place, learning to utilize the frost that permeated that land as a way to uphold their task. The Greatwolf quickly established itself as the leader among the other wolves as well, commanding them and likely using them as guards of the tomb as well.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:

 trivia : The word "**大狼**", which means a "Great Wolf", was also used in *Dark Souls* as part of Sif's title.
The translation of the Greatwolf's name may cause a bit of confusion: the Greatwolf is just a pet of the Gravetender, not a Gravetender itself.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet:
Unlike the Gravetender, who remains in the arena at all times, the Greatwolf can be encountered earlier on as a powerful miniboss-like encounter, fighting alongside a rather numerous pack of smaller wolves. It has the same abilities as in the boss battle, but unlike in that fight, its health must not be depleated fully, as it will flee after less than half of it has been removed.

If the player defeats the Greatwolf in these two encounters, they will receive three Large Titanite Shard with each victory. This also has the added bonus of lowering its boss fight health by 10% with each time it is beaten.The effect will not reset if the player dies on their first attempt of the boss battle, meaning it is permanently weakened. Beating it with the Gravetender before defeating it in the other areas of Ariandel will make it disappear from those locations, meaning the Large Titanite Shards cannot be obtained any longer.

snippet:
Corvian -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Corvians are almost completely vulnerable before starting their transformation. However, if they have already started it and are attacked, the transformation will complete immediately, rendering them able to retaliate. They stagger easily, though, and fast weapons like straight swords should leave them with no opportunity to counterattack. If a heavy weapon is used, the player should make sure that the corvian will die in one or two hits.

It is not advisable to engage more than one of these creatures at a time due to the constant damage output they can deal and their quick recovery times. If they are found congregated in front of a storyteller, either the latter should be dealt first or each corvian should be drawn in individually with ranged attacks. In some cases, if the storyteller dies, all remaining corvians will become completely oblivious to the player, making for easy kills.

 description : Hunchbacked, foul medium-sized creatures, hybrids between a hollow and a crow, and armed with either a dagger or a scythe. Corvians initially stand on their posts and barely attack or move from place until approached. When this happens, however, they will begin a brief transformation in which two pairs of wings extrude from their backs, one at a time. When they finish, they will become extremely aggressive, being able to chase the player for long distances. They will also gain the ability to fly in short bursts and attack with a rapid barrage of claw-swipes with their legs.

In some cases, a group of corvians can be found congregated around a Corvian Storyteller. If the storyteller spots the player, it will unleash a shivering shriek that will alert the rest of the flock, making all corvians in the vicinity begin their transformations and then rush toward the player in unison.

snippet:
Corvian Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Corvian Knights are incredibly agile opponents and will regularly backflip away or leap over the player to disorient them, often following up with a lunging stab. This can be punished by dodging and backstabbing. Their flurry of blade attacks can rapidly inflict bleed, even when guarding through a shield, so it's not recommended to attempt to block their strikes. From a distance, they will throw several knives and will often perform this attack if the player attempts to heal or use an item.

The robed Corvian Knights will pursue and eliminate the lesser Corvians around the settlement, although they will focus on the player if alerted. The variant wielding talons is often encountered hiding upside down under bridges and ceilings, so it is advisable for the player to be mindful of their surroundings.

title: Ariamis
snippet:
Ariamis -  Dark Souls - character - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that Ariamis is strongly affiliated with the Gods of Anor Londo. To create the painting he had to use the First Flame and the Dark Soul, both powers kept under control by the gods. Furthermore, the painting was kept in Anor Londo, implying that even if the gods themselves had not commissioned it, the product of Ariamis' work was known and available to them. This also implies that the gods had placed a lot of trust in Ariamis to freely manipulate the First Flame and the Dark Soul and that they possess uncommon magical abilities to understand these primordial powers and use them to shape nested worlds.

title: Ariamis
snippet:
Ariamis -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Although Ariamis's name and figure were eventually lost to history, their knowledge on the nature of Painted Worlds was passed down. In the following iterations of Paintings, the natives of Painted Worlds possessed a proficient understanding of the First Flame and the Dark Soul. Whenever their world showed signs of corruption, they used the Flame to "restore" the Painting, to avoid the fate of the stagnating outside world. For this purpose the corvians chose a "Father" who presided over the Flame and would burn away their home when the time came. After the Flame was unleashed, a painter like Ariamis would use the Dark Soul as pigment to create a new painting.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

 irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo : On the surface, the Ashen One fights their way to the grand church in Irithyll where they find Pontiff Sulyvahn. Killing Sulyvahn opens the way to Anor Londo, fabled city of the gods, where Aldrich awaits. Aldrich, having lost interest in the flame and having instead turned towards the Dark, sought out Anor Londo to devour the gods themselves. He found and devoured Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo, who had been "stricken by illness" and had retreated to the Anor Londo Cathedral, only to be imprisoned by the Pontiff to be fed to Aldrich. Fighting their way past the archers protecting the city, the Ashen One finds Aldrich using Gwyndolin as a puppet of sorts, and kills him, acquiring his ashes to be delivered to his throne.

 dark_souls_iii : In the time of Lothric, more Corvians are seen outside the painting, some of them even acting as storytellers who share tales of their frigid home. Their stories are considered heretical, and most of their listeners are Corvians themselves. All of them have no place to go, and seemingly yearn to return to the frozen landscape of their painting.

These aren't the only descendants of the Crow People, however, and many of them still exist within a new Painted World, restored by Father Ariandel. He appears to be a large humanoid akin to a Giant, but shows some crow-like features across his body, like fuzzy legs and talon-like hands. It's unclear if he was one of the Corvians, but he was one of the more important figures of their society. The most important one by far was the mistress of the Painted World, who wielded a great scythe, which became a symbol of a long-lost home to the forlorn corvids.

title: Corvian (Lore)

 dark_souls_ii : By the time of Drangleic, knowledge of the Painted World had been lost. Regardless, some of its Corvian inhabitants took their leave, as one of their descendants, Weaponsmith Ornifex, can be found in the old town of Tseldora. Her choice to live in Tseldora seems rather curious, as the town has some passing connection to the ancient Goddess of Sin. It's unclear if she even knows of her and how relevant she used to be to her people.

She uses a special forging technique that originated from a strange being that once inhabited the area, though she is unaware of what it truly was. She also believes humans to be inherently different than her kind, suggesting that across the ages, the Crow People had forgotten that they originated from humans. This was probably not helped by the general distrust humanity displays when dealing with creatures who are different than them.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: Now, many of the Corvian Settlers are being slaughtered by their knights for disagreeing with Friede's decision, and the people's opinion of her had turned sour. The Corvians suffered under the effects of the rot, many shriveling up, unable to move their legs, or festering with poison. Most of them drag tails made of feces, strung together by undigested plant matter. Only the coming of a second Ash can set things right, and that is what the forlorn Corvians and other inhabitants of the Painted World desire more than anything.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Corvians are transformed humans, warped by their obsessive devotion to Velka, Goddess of Sin. They are surprisingly varied in appearance, varying in how humanoid or bird-like they are. The earliest ones had lanky, androgynous bodies with crow heads, large wings replacing their arms, and red feet, while the later ones looked like emaciated humanoids with feathered legs and bird-like feet, capable of sprouting wings separate from their arms, though they lacked any real corvid feature in their faces. Lastly, most of the ones living in the painting, deprived of wings and sporting a few scattered feathers, but with an undeniable bird head with desaturated white eyes. Their knights are like a mix of this latter type and the very first one, showing a lanky yet imposing frame, while having no wings of their own. They are characterized as being unwanted, forlorn beings with no place to call home.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet: She is also the only Corvian that can be met in Drangleic, found in the clutches of the Lion Clan, who live in the nearby Shaded Woods. It's very likely more Corvians were travelling the world, but they are never met by the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Corvians have humble beginnings. Once, they were simple human worshippers of the Goddess Velka, who transformed through their devotion. In the time of Lordran, they were best known as Crow People of Velka, or simply Crow Demons. Despite being called "demons", they share no relation with the Chaos Demons of Izalith, as they were ultimately human in nature.

At some point, these devotees would find themselves in the Painted World of Ariamis, either banished there or simply seeking an escape from the real world, along with many of Velka's artifacts and a peculiar crossbreed child. Whether they transformed before setting foot within the painting or afterwards is unclear, but their presence was entirely localized within the frigid landscape, with none of them found elsewhere in this age. They are hostile to all those who enter the painting and don't belong there.
